Karthik —

Initial findings from the ingress proxies (us-west-2):
- Observed a spike in TLS handshake duration distribution starting 07:48 PST; 95th percentile jumped from ~20ms -> ~680ms.
- Session cache miss rate increased ~6x for a subset of upstream egress nodes in the transit mesh.
- A recent TLS library upgrade was rolled to the transit proxies yesterday in the canary pool; code itself fine but we see unexpected renegotiation behavior under connection churn.
- Packet capture (attached as transit-mesh-handshake-trace.txt) shows repeated full-handshakes where resumptions should occur.

Mitigation attempted (08:30 PST):
- Increased TLS session cache size on the affected proxies — reduced handshake durations on ~60% of flows but Novum still hits tail in certain AZs.
- We can fail Novum to the older non-mesh ingress (manual route) as a short-term bypass — requires platform approval.

Action items:
1) Rollback TLS library change in transit canary -> if confirms, schedule full rollback to older build (ETA 45 mins).
2) Open temporary route for Novum to non-mesh ingress (manual rule) — requires Ops approval and IP allowlist update (ETA 15 mins once approved).
3) Correlate with cloud provider peering metrics for any packet retransmission bursts.

I'll continue with packet-level triage and will post an update in 20 mins.

-Marissa
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Subject: Exec brief: Novum outage risk — transit mesh TLS session churn (need go/no-go for bypass)

Vivek —

Novum (large retail customer) is experiencing production checkout failures tied to TLS handshake tail latency that cascades into 5xx errors. SREs traced this to increased TLS full-handshakes in our transit mesh after a library change in the last canary roll. Impact is highest in a small set of us-west AZs; overall request error rate for Novum has doubled in the last 30m.

Options on the table (tradeoffs):
- Rollback canary to previous TLS build across transit proxies (risk: deployment rollback time ~45m, may cause transient reconnects).
- Route Novum to non-mesh ingress (bypass transit mesh) — fastest fix (~15-30m) but bypasses some DDoS/e2e observability hooks and requires temporary ACL updates and an ops change freeze lift.
- Continue scaling session cache and keep monitoring — may not address tail for affected AZs promptly.

Recommended immediate action: approve manual bypass for Novum to restore their checkout (we can re-enable once rollback completes). Also execute a full rollback of TLS library from canary to avoid recurrence.

Customer asks: ETA to restore checkout flows. They're pressing for credits if recovery time exceeds 2 hours. Please advise on approval for bypass + rollback.

-Karthik
